# Plan: Expand `docs/tools/tmux.md` (resources, vim integration, theme alternatives, bandwidth bug)

## Context

The user wants to enrich `docs/tools/tmux.md` with:

1. Two external references (awesome-tmux list, SmartBear tmux+vim article).
2. A discussion of tmux × vim integration. They want to confirm whether the current config already gives vi-style scroll/copy mode (it does — see below).
3. Notes on alternative themes / status-bar layouts, inspired by [omerxx's dotfiles](https://github.com/omerxx/dotfiles/tree/master/tmux) and [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GH3kpsbbERo) where windows/tabs are rendered on the **top** status line with a Catppuccin-style theme.
4. A troubleshooting note for the broken bandwidth segment — the status bar shows `18446744073709551615K` (= `2^64 − 1`, classic uint64 underflow) instead of real network throughput.

## Findings from current config (`dot_tmux.conf`)

- Vi copy-mode is already wired up:
  - `setw -g mode-keys vi` (line 62)
  - `bind -T copy-mode-vi v / V / C-v / y` (lines 165–174)
  - `prefix + [` enters copy mode; `h/j/k/l`, `g/G`, `C-u/C-d`, `/`, `?` all behave vim-style.
  - So **yes**, scroll + copy are already vim-flavored. Doc just needs to make this explicit in the new "tmux × vim" section (the existing copy-mode table already covers it; we'll cross-reference).
- Theme is `tmux2k` with `onedark` (line 39–49), status bar pinned to **bottom** (`status-position bottom`, line 77).
- Bandwidth segment comes from `@tmux2k-right-plugins "bandwidth network time"` (line 49). The `18446744073709551615K` symptom is a known tmux2k issue where the bandwidth script's counter delta underflows (network interface auto-detection picks the wrong iface, or the cached previous counter is missing on first tick, causing `(prev - curr)` to wrap on uint64). See tmux2k issues #29 / #41.

## Changes — all in `docs/tools/tmux.md`

### 1. Add a "Resources" section near the bottom (before "Related Docs")

\```markdown
## Resources

- [rothgar/awesome-tmux](https://github.com/rothgar/awesome-tmux) — curated list of tmux plugins, themes, and articles.
- [Tmux and Vim — even better together (SmartBear)](https://smartbear.com/blog/tmux-and-vim/) — workflow patterns for pairing tmux with vim/Neovim.
- [omerxx/dotfiles — tmux/](https://github.com/omerxx/dotfiles/tree/master/tmux) — reference config with Catppuccin theme and top status bar (see [video walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GH3kpsbbERo)).
\```

### 2. Expand the existing "Coding-Agent / Neovim Notes" section, OR add a new "Tmux × Vim / Neovim" subsection

Add a short subsection that:

- Confirms vi-style copy/scroll is already on (`mode-keys vi`, `prefix + [`, `v` / `V` / `C-v` / `y`, `/` `?`, `g`/`G`, `C-u`/`C-d`).
- Cross-links to the existing **Copy Mode (Vim-Style)** table above instead of repeating it.
- Mentions options not currently installed but worth knowing:
  - [`christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator`](https://github.com/christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator) for unified `Ctrl+h/j/k/l` pane↔split navigation between tmux and (Neo)vim. Note: would conflict with our prefix-less navigation expectations; document as opt-in.
  - `focus-events on` is already set (line 73) — required for vim's `autoread` and Neovim's `FocusGained`.
  - True color + extended keys are already configured (lines 136–145), so vim colorschemes and `<C-_>` / `<S-CR>` work inside tmux.
- Links to the SmartBear article for broader workflow ideas.

### 3. Add an "Alternative Themes & Status Bar Layout" section

Document, without changing the default config:

- Current: tmux2k onedark, bottom status bar.
- Alternative inspired by omerxx: [`catppuccin/tmux`](https://github.com/catppuccin/tmux) with `set -g status-position top` and window list on the top bar. Useful when running coding agents at the bottom of the screen so the status doesn't hop when output scrolls.
- Other themes already commented out in `dot_tmux.conf` (lines 291–297): `dracula/tmux`, `wfxr/tmux-power`, `ndyakov/pimux`, `thewtex/tmux-mem-cpu-load`.
- Snippet (for reference, not applied):

  \```tmux
  set -g @plugin 'catppuccin/tmux'
  set -g @catppuccin_flavour 'mocha'
  set -g status-position top
  \```

### 4. Add a "Troubleshooting" section with a `Bandwidth shows 18446744073709551615K` entry

Explain:

- The number is `UINT64_MAX` (`2^64 − 1`), produced when tmux2k's bandwidth helper computes `prev − current` and underflows. This happens when:
  - tmux2k auto-picks an interface that has no traffic / disappears (VPN, docker0, etc.), or
  - the cached previous-tick counter is missing on first refresh after reload.
- Workarounds (pick one):
  1. Pin the interface explicitly:

     \```tmux
     set -g @tmux2k-network-name "en0"   # macOS Wi-Fi; use `ip -br link` / `ifconfig` to find yours
     \```

  2. Drop `bandwidth` from `@tmux2k-right-plugins` if you don't need it.
  3. Switch to a different status segment, e.g. tmux-plugins/tmux-net-speed, or move to Catppuccin (see Alternative Themes).
- Reference upstream issues: [tmux2k#29](https://github.com/2kabhishek/tmux2k/issues/29), [#41](https://github.com/2kabhishek/tmux2k/issues/41) (link as "see upstream tmux2k issues" without claiming exact issue numbers if uncertain at write-time).

## Files to modify

- `docs/tools/tmux.md` — only file edited. No code/config changes in this plan; the `dot_tmux.conf` bandwidth fix is left as a follow-up the user can choose (pin interface vs drop segment vs switch theme).

可以，而且其實 很好做。
最實用的方式不是在同一份設定裡硬切，而是做成：
	•	一份共用設定 tmux.common.conf
	•	一份 theme.catppuccin.conf
	•	一份 theme.tmux2k.conf
	•	主設定 tmux.conf 只負責「讀哪一份 theme」

這樣最乾淨，也最好除錯。

⸻

我推薦的結構

~/.config/tmux/
├── tmux.conf
├── tmux.common.conf
├── theme.catppuccin.conf
└── theme.tmux2k.conf


⸻

1. 主入口 tmux.conf

用 tmux option 當開關：

# ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf

# 共用基礎設定
source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.common.conf

# 預設主題
set -g @theme_variant "catppuccin"

# 根據變數切換
if -F '#{==:#{@theme_variant},catppuccin}' \
  'source-file ~/.config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf'

if -F '#{==:#{@theme_variant},tmux2k}' \
  'source-file ~/.config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf'


⸻

2. 共用設定 tmux.common.conf

把兩邊都共用的東西放這裡：

# ~/.config/tmux/tmux.common.conf

set -g mouse on
set -g default-terminal "tmux-256color"
set -g history-limit 100000
set -g status-position bottom

bind r source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf \; display-message "tmux config reloaded"

# 快速切換 theme
bind C source-file ~/.config/tmux/switch-to-catppuccin.conf
bind T source-file ~/.config/tmux/switch-to-tmux2k.conf

這裡我順便綁：
	•	prefix + r：reload
	•	prefix + C：切到 catppuccin
	•	prefix + T：切到 tmux2k

⸻

3. 切換腳本

switch-to-catppuccin.conf

set -g @theme_variant "catppuccin"
source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf
display-message "Switched to catppuccin"

switch-to-tmux2k.conf

set -g @theme_variant "tmux2k"
source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf
display-message "Switched to tmux2k"


⸻

4. theme.catppuccin.conf

# ~/.config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf

# 先清掉可能衝突的 status 設定
set -g status-left ""
set -g status-right ""
set -g window-status-format ""
set -g window-status-current-format ""

# Catppuccin options
set -g @catppuccin_flavor "mocha"
set -g @catppuccin_window_status_style "rounded"

# 如果你是手動安裝
run ~/.config/tmux/plugins/catppuccin/tmux/catppuccin.tmux

# 或 TPM 版
# run ~/.tmux/plugins/catppuccin/tmux/catppuccin.tmux

# 自己想要的 modules
set -g status-left ""
set -g status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_application}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_session}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_uptime}"


⸻

5. theme.tmux2k.conf

# ~/.config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf

# 先清掉可能衝突的 status 設定
set -g status-left ""
set -g status-right ""
set -g window-status-format ""
set -g window-status-current-format ""

# tmux2k options
set -g @tmux2k-theme "catppuccin"
set -g @tmux2k-icons-only false
set -g @tmux2k-show-powerline true

run ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux2k/2k.tmux


⸻

6. TPM 寫法怎麼放

如果你用 TPM，兩個 plugin 都可以先裝著：

set -g @plugin 'catppuccin/tmux'
set -g @plugin '2kabhishek/tmux2k'
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tpm'
run '~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/tpm'

重點是：
	•	安裝可以同時存在
	•	啟用時只 source 對應那一份

不要兩個 theme 都在主設定裡直接 run，不然很容易互蓋。

⸻

7. 最穩的切換方式

如果你發現切換後有殘留樣式，這很正常，因為 tmux 有些 option 是持久的。
所以最穩的方法有兩種。

方法 A：同一 session 內 reload

方便、快，但偶爾會有殘留。

方法 B：開新 tmux server

最乾淨：

tmux kill-server
tmux

如果你很在意一致性，建議把「試 theme」和「日常用」分開。

⸻

8. 更進一步：用 shell 環境變數切換

你也可以從 shell 啟動時決定：

if-shell '[ "$TMUX_THEME" = "tmux2k" ]' \
  'set -g @theme_variant "tmux2k"' \
  'set -g @theme_variant "catppuccin"'

然後：

TMUX_THEME=tmux2k tmux

這種很適合你用不同 script / alias 啟動不同風格。

例如：

alias tmuxc='TMUX_THEME=catppuccin tmux'
alias tmuxt='TMUX_THEME=tmux2k tmux'


⸻

9. 我最推薦你用的版本

以你的習慣，我會推薦：
	•	平常主力：catppuccin
	•	想展示或試 UI：tmux2k

然後做成：
	•	prefix + C → catppuccin
	•	prefix + T → tmux2k
	•	prefix + r → reload

這樣最順手。

⸻

10. 一個現實提醒

這兩個都會動到：
	•	status-left
	•	status-right
	•	window-status-format
	•	window-status-current-format
	•	各種顏色/樣式 option

所以共用設定不要碰 status bar 細節，只放：
	•	mouse
	•	terminal
	•	prefix
	•	pane/navigation keybindings
	•	history-limit
	•	base-index
	•	vi mode

theme 專屬的東西全放進各自檔案。

⸻

```md
# Plan: Modularize tmux config + switchable Catppuccin / tmux2k themes, doc updates

## Context

User wants to extend the current tmux setup in three coordinated ways:

1. **Refactor the monolithic `dot_tmux.conf`** into a modular directory layout so shared settings and per-theme settings are cleanly separated.
2. **Add a second theme (Catppuccin + top status bar)** inspired by [omerxx/dotfiles](https://github.com/omerxx/dotfiles/tree/master/tmux) / [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GH3kpsbbERo), and make it the **default**. Keep tmux2k as an opt-in alternative, selectable via env var **or** runtime key-binding.
3. **Expand `docs/tools/tmux.md`** with: the two reference links the user supplied, a tmux × Neovim section (confirming the existing vi-style copy/scroll support), the new theme-switch mechanics, and a troubleshooting entry for the tmux2k bandwidth bug (`18446744073709551615K` = `UINT64_MAX` underflow).

The bandwidth bug will be **documented only**, not patched in config (per user answer).

## Findings from current `dot_tmux.conf`

- vi copy-mode is already wired: `mode-keys vi` (line 62) + `v / V / C-v / y / g / G / / / ?` (lines 165–180). Doc just needs to cross-reference it in the new Vim section — no config change.
- Theme = `tmux2k` onedark, status-position **bottom** (lines 39–49, 77).
- TPM path is `~/.tmux/plugins` (line 9). After refactor, we should keep that path (standard) even though the main config moves to `~/.config/tmux/`.
- Bandwidth segment comes from `@tmux2k-right-plugins "bandwidth network time"` (line 49). UINT64 underflow is a known tmux2k issue (bandwidth script's `prev − curr` wraps on first tick / when iface changes).
- Commented-out alternative themes exist at lines 291–297 (dracula, tmux-power, pimux, mem-cpu-load) — safe to drop during refactor; we're adding proper Catppuccin support.

## Target layout (chezmoi source → deployed path)

\```
chezmoi:  dot_config/tmux/                  →  ~/.config/tmux/
          ├── tmux.conf                     (entry point, selects theme)
          ├── common.conf                   (everything theme-agnostic)
          ├── keybindings.conf              (all bind-key / popup menu)
          ├── theme.catppuccin.conf         (new — default)
          └── theme.tmux2k.conf             (existing theme, moved)
\```

The legacy `dot_tmux.conf` (→ `~/.tmux.conf`) becomes a one-line shim so existing users / scripts that `source ~/.tmux.conf` keep working:

\```tmux
# ~/.tmux.conf — shim: delegate to XDG location
source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf
\```

Rationale: tmux auto-reads `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` on modern versions, but keeping the shim avoids breaking anything that references `~/.tmux.conf` (e.g. the `prefix + R` reload binding, install scripts, the `Verify Current Config` snippet in the doc).

## File-by-file plan

### `dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf` (new entry point)

\```tmux
# Shared base (no status/theme styling)
source-file ~/.config/tmux/common.conf
source-file ~/.config/tmux/keybindings.conf

# Theme selection — priority:
#   1. TMUX_THEME env var (catppuccin | tmux2k)
#   2. tmux option @theme_variant (persisted across reload within server)
#   3. default: catppuccin
if-shell '[ -n "$TMUX_THEME" ]' \
  'set -g @theme_variant "$TMUX_THEME"'
if-shell '[ -z "#{@theme_variant}" ]' \
  'set -g @theme_variant "catppuccin"'

if -F '#{==:#{@theme_variant},catppuccin}' \
  'source-file ~/.config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf'
if -F '#{==:#{@theme_variant},tmux2k}' \
  'source-file ~/.config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf'

# TPM init must be last
run 'PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin:$PATH" ~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/tpm'
\```

### `dot_config/tmux/common.conf` (new — theme-agnostic)

Contains, lifted verbatim from `dot_tmux.conf`:

- TPM env + `set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tpm'`
- Non-theme plugins: `tmux-resurrect`, `tmux-continuum`, `tmux-floax` (+ floax options), `tmux-fzf-url`, `tmux-open` (+ `@open-S`)
- General settings: `escape-time 0`, `mouse on`, `mode-keys vi`, `history-limit 50000`, `base-index 1`, `pane-base-index 1`, `renumber-windows on`, `focus-events on`, `detach-on-destroy off`
- Terminal/keys: `default-terminal tmux-256color`, `terminal-features RGB`, `extended-keys always`, csi-u conditional, `set-clipboard on`, `allow-passthrough on`
- **Both** theme plugins declared (so TPM installs both; only one is activated):
  \```tmux
  set -g @plugin 'catppuccin/tmux'
  set -g @plugin '2kabhishek/tmux2k'
  \```
- **Not** included here: `status-position`, `status-left/right`, `window-status-*`, any color/style — those belong to the theme files.

### `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` (new — all bindings & popup menu)

Moved verbatim from `dot_tmux.conf`:

- Copy-mode vi bindings (v/V/C-v/y, mouse drag, double-click)
- Capture pane helpers (`y`, `Y`, `C-y`)
- Pane/window: `h/j/k/l`, `H/J/K/L`, `M-h/j/k/l`, `|`, `-`, `+`, `c`, `x`, `R`, `N`, `X`
- Sesh: `g`, `S`, `9`
- Popup menu (`prefix + Space`) — full `display-menu` block
- **New**: `prefix + C` → switch to catppuccin, `prefix + T` → switch to tmux2k:
  \```tmux
  bind C run-shell 'tmux set -g @theme_variant catppuccin; \
    tmux source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf; \
    tmux display-message "Theme: catppuccin"'
  bind T run-shell 'tmux set -g @theme_variant tmux2k; \
    tmux source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf; \
    tmux display-message "Theme: tmux2k"'
  \```
  Add corresponding rows to the popup menu ("Theme: catppuccin" / "Theme: tmux2k").

### `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` (new — default)

\```tmux
# Reset any inherited status styling
set -g status-left ""
set -g status-right ""
set -g window-status-format ""
set -g window-status-current-format ""

# Top status bar (omerxx-style)
set -g status-position top

# Catppuccin options
set -g @catppuccin_flavor "mocha"
set -g @catppuccin_window_status_style "rounded"

# Load plugin (TPM install path)
run '~/.tmux/plugins/tmux/catppuccin.tmux'

# Compose status line
set -g status-left "#{E:@catppuccin_status_session} "
set -g status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_application}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_uptime}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_date_time}"
\```

Exact modules/flavour are easy to tweak after first render; the key invariants are `status-position top` and Catppuccin being self-contained.

### `dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf` (new — lifted from current config)

\```tmux
# Reset so toggling from catppuccin leaves no residue
set -g status-left ""
set -g status-right ""
set -g window-status-format ""
set -g window-status-current-format ""
set -g status-position bottom

set -g @tmux2k-theme 'onedark'
set -g @tmux2k-start-icon ""
set -g @tmux2k-left-plugins "git cpu ram"
set -g @tmux2k-right-plugins "bandwidth network time"

run '~/.tmux/plugins/tmux2k/tmux2k.tmux'

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Modularize tmux config + switchable Catppuccin / tmux2k themes, doc updates

## Context

User wants to extend the current tmux setup in three coordinated ways:

1. **Refactor the monolithic `dot_tmux.conf`** into a modular directory layout so shared settings and per-theme settings are cleanly separated.
2. **Add a second theme (Catppuccin + top status bar)** inspired by [omerxx/dotfiles](https://github.com/omerxx/dotfiles/tree/master/tmux) / [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GH3kpsbbERo), and make it the **default**. Keep tmux2k as an opt-in alternative, selectable via env var **or** runtime key-binding.
3. **Expand `docs/tools/tmux.md`** with: the two reference links the user supplied, a tmux × Neovim section (confirming the existing vi-style copy/scroll support), the new theme-switch mechanics, and a troubleshooting entry for the tmux2k bandwidth bug (`18446744073709551615K` = `UINT64_MAX` underflow).

The bandwidth bug will be **documented only**, not patched in config (per user answer).

## Findings from current `dot_tmux.conf`

- vi copy-mode is already wired: `mode-keys vi` (line 62) + `v / V / C-v / y / g / G / / / ?` (lines 165–180). Doc just needs to cross-reference it in the new Vim section — no config change.
- Theme = `tmux2k` onedark, status-position **bottom** (lines 39–49, 77).
- TPM path is `~/.tmux/plugins` (line 9). After refactor, we should keep that path (standard) even though the main config moves to `~/.config/tmux/`.
- Bandwidth segment comes from `@tmux2k-right-plugins "bandwidth network time"` (line 49). UINT64 underflow is a known tmux2k issue (bandwidth script's `prev − curr` wraps on first tick / when iface changes).
- Commented-out alternative themes exist at lines 291–297 (dracula, tmux-power, pimux, mem-cpu-load) — safe to drop during refactor; we're adding proper Catppuccin support.

## Target layout (chezmoi source → deployed path)

```
chezmoi:  dot_config/tmux/                  →  ~/.config/tmux/
          ├── tmux.conf                     (entry point, selects theme)
          ├── common.conf                   (everything theme-agnostic)
          ├── keybindings.conf              (all bind-key / popup menu)
          ├── theme.catppuccin.conf         (new — default)
          └── theme.tmux2k.conf             (existing theme, moved)
```

The legacy `dot_tmux.conf` (→ `~/.tmux.conf`) becomes a one-line shim so existing users / scripts that `source ~/.tmux.conf` keep working:

```tmux
# ~/.tmux.conf — shim: delegate to XDG location
source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf
```

Rationale: tmux auto-reads `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` on modern versions, but keeping the shim avoids breaking anything that references `~/.tmux.conf` (e.g. the `prefix + R` reload binding, install scripts, the `Verify Current Config` snippet in the doc).

## File-by-file plan

### `dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf` (new entry point)

```tmux
# Shared base (no status/theme styling)
source-file ~/.config/tmux/common.conf
source-file ~/.config/tmux/keybindings.conf

# Theme selection — priority:
#   1. TMUX_THEME env var (catppuccin | tmux2k)
#   2. tmux option @theme_variant (persisted across reload within server)
#   3. default: catppuccin
if-shell '[ -n "$TMUX_THEME" ]' \
  'set -g @theme_variant "$TMUX_THEME"'
if-shell '[ -z "#{@theme_variant}" ]' \
  'set -g @theme_variant "catppuccin"'

if -F '#{==:#{@theme_variant},catppuccin}' \
  'source-file ~/.config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf'
if -F '#{==:#{@theme_variant},tmux2k}' \
  'source-file ~/.config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf'

# TPM init must be last
run 'PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin:$PATH" ~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/tpm'
```

### `dot_config/tmux/common.conf` (new — theme-agnostic)

Contains, lifted verbatim from `dot_tmux.conf`:

- TPM env + `set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tpm'`
- Non-theme plugins: `tmux-resurrect`, `tmux-continuum`, `tmux-floax` (+ floax options), `tmux-fzf-url`, `tmux-open` (+ `@open-S`)
- General settings: `escape-time 0`, `mouse on`, `mode-keys vi`, `history-limit 50000`, `base-index 1`, `pane-base-index 1`, `renumber-windows on`, `focus-events on`, `detach-on-destroy off`
- Terminal/keys: `default-terminal tmux-256color`, `terminal-features RGB`, `extended-keys always`, csi-u conditional, `set-clipboard on`, `allow-passthrough on`
- **Both** theme plugins declared (so TPM installs both; only one is activated):
  ```tmux
  set -g @plugin 'catppuccin/tmux'
  set -g @plugin '2kabhishek/tmux2k'
  ```
- **Not** included here: `status-position`, `status-left/right`, `window-status-*`, any color/style — those belong to the theme files.

### `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` (new — all bindings & popup menu)

Moved verbatim from `dot_tmux.conf`:

- **New**: `prefix + C` → switch to catppuccin, `prefix + T` → switch to tmux2k:

  bind T run-shell 'tmux set -g @theme_variant tmux2k; \

  ```
  Add corresponding rows to the popup menu ("Theme: catppuccin" / "Theme: tmux2k").

### `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` (new — default)

```tmux
# Reset any inherited status styling
set -g status-left ""
set -g status-right ""
set -g window-status-format ""
set -g window-status-current-format ""

# Top status bar (omerxx-style)
set -g status-position top

# Catppuccin options
set -g @catppuccin_flavor "mocha"
set -g @catppuccin_window_status_style "rounded"

# Load plugin (TPM install path)
run '~/.tmux/plugins/tmux/catppuccin.tmux'

# Compose status line
set -g status-left "#{E:@catppuccin_status_session} "
set -g status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_application}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_uptime}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_date_time}"
```

Exact modules/flavour are easy to tweak after first render; the key invariants are `status-position top` and Catppuccin being self-contained.

set -g status-position bottom

# ~/.config/tmux/common.conf
# Theme-agnostic settings: plugins, general options, terminal compatibility.
# Managed by chezmoi - do not edit directly.

# =============================================================================
# Plugins (managed by TPM; theme plugins live in theme.*.conf)
# =============================================================================

set-environment -g TMUX_PLUGIN_MANAGER_PATH '~/.tmux/plugins'

set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tpm'

# Session management
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-resurrect'
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-continuum'

# Floating scratch pane (prefix + F to toggle, prefix + P for menu)
set -g @plugin 'omerxx/tmux-floax'
set -g @floax-bind 'F'
set -g @floax-bind-menu 'P'
set -g @floax-width '80%'
set -g @floax-height '80%'
set -g @floax-border-color 'magenta'
set -g @floax-text-color 'blue'
set -g @floax-session-name 'float'
set -g @floax-change-path 'true'

# URL picker: prefix + u opens fzf popup with all URLs in the pane
set -g @plugin 'joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url'

# Open highlighted selection in copy-mode: o = open, C-o = open in $EDITOR, S = search
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-open'
set -g @open-S 'https://www.google.com/search?q='

# =============================================================================
# General Settings
# =============================================================================

# No ESC delay (critical for Neovim and coding agents)
set -sg escape-time 0

# Enable mouse support
setw -g mouse on

# Use vi mode keys in copy mode
setw -g mode-keys vi

# Larger scrollback buffer
set -g history-limit 50000

# 1-indexed windows and panes
set -g base-index 1
setw -g pane-base-index 1
set -g renumber-windows on

# Focus events for Vim autoread compatibility
set -g focus-events on

# If the current session is destroyed, switch to another one instead of detaching
set -g detach-on-destroy off

# Status bar visibility (position is set per-theme)
set-option -g status on

# =============================================================================
# Terminal & Key Compatibility
# =============================================================================

set -s default-terminal 'tmux-256color'
set -as terminal-features ",xterm-256color:RGB"

# Forward extended keys (CSI-u) so Ctrl+/, Shift+Enter etc. reach TUIs
set -s extended-keys always
if-shell 'tmux -V | grep -qE "tmux ([3-9]\.[5-9]|[3-9]\.[1-9][0-9]|[4-9]\.)"' \
  'set -s extended-keys-format csi-u'
set -as terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'

# OSC 52 clipboard (works over SSH)
set -g set-clipboard on

# Allow OSC passthrough (for terminal images, sixel, etc.)
set -g allow-passthrough on

```

```conf
# ~/.config/tmux/keybindings.conf
# All bind-key definitions and the prefix + Space popup menu.
# Managed by chezmoi - do not edit directly.

# =============================================================================
# Vim-Style Copy Mode (prefix + [ to enter, q to exit)
# =============================================================================
#
#   h/j/k/l  move cursor        C-u/C-d  half-page up/down
#   g/G      top/bottom          //?      search forward/backward
#   v        begin selection     V        line selection
#   C-v      rectangle select    y        yank to clipboard
#   Escape   clear selection     q        exit copy mode

bind -T copy-mode-vi v send-keys -X begin-selection
bind -T copy-mode-vi V send-keys -X select-line
bind -T copy-mode-vi C-v send-keys -X rectangle-toggle
bind -T copy-mode-vi y send-keys -X copy-selection-and-cancel
bind -T copy-mode-vi MouseDragEnd1Pane send-keys -X copy-selection
bind -T copy-mode-vi DoubleClick1Pane select-pane \; send-keys -X select-word

# =============================================================================
# Capture Pane Helpers
# =============================================================================

# prefix + y: copy visible pane content to system clipboard
bind y run-shell "\
  if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then \
    tmux capture-pane -p | pbcopy; \
  elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then \
    tmux capture-pane -p | xclip -selection clipboard; \
  elif command -v xsel >/dev/null; then \
    tmux capture-pane -p | xsel --clipboard; \
  fi; \
  tmux display-message 'Pane content copied to clipboard'"

# prefix + Y: copy full scrollback to system clipboard
bind Y run-shell "\
  if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then \
    tmux capture-pane -pS - | pbcopy; \
  elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then \
    tmux capture-pane -pS - | xclip -selection clipboard; \
  elif command -v xsel >/dev/null; then \
    tmux capture-pane -pS - | xsel --clipboard; \
  fi; \
  tmux display-message 'Full scrollback copied to clipboard'"

# prefix + C-y: capture pane into fzf for line-by-line selection, yank chosen lines
bind C-y run-shell "\
  clip() { \
    if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then pbcopy; \
    elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then xclip -selection clipboard; \
    elif command -v xsel >/dev/null; then xsel --clipboard; \
    fi; \
  }; \
  tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% --multi --tac --no-sort \
    --header 'Select lines to copy (Tab=multi, Enter=copy)' | clip; \
  tmux display-message 'Selected lines copied'"

# =============================================================================
# Vim-Style Pane Navigation
# =============================================================================

bind h select-pane -L
bind j select-pane -D
bind k select-pane -U
bind l select-pane -R

# Intuitive split bindings (| = left/right, - = top/bottom)
bind | split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}"
bind - split-window -v -c "#{pane_current_path}"

# Resize panes with prefix + H/J/K/L (5 cells)
bind -r H resize-pane -L 5
bind -r J resize-pane -D 5
bind -r K resize-pane -U 5
bind -r L resize-pane -R 5

# Fine resize with Meta + h/j/k/l (1 cell, repeatable)
bind -r M-h resize-pane -L 1
bind -r M-j resize-pane -D 1
bind -r M-k resize-pane -U 1
bind -r M-l resize-pane -R 1

# Quick ratio: set current pane to 75% width
bind + resize-pane -x 75%

# New window/pane inherits current path
bind c new-window -c "#{pane_current_path}"

# Reload config with prefix + R
bind R source-file "$HOME/.tmux.conf" \; display-message "Sourced ~/.tmux.conf"

# Session management
bind N command-prompt -p "New session:" "new-session -s '%%'"
bind X confirm-before -p "Kill session #S? (y/n)" kill-session
bind x confirm-before -p "Kill pane? (y/n)" kill-pane

# =============================================================================
# Theme Switching (Catppuccin <-> tmux2k)
# =============================================================================
# Note: first-time switch requires `prefix + I` to install the target plugin.

bind C run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant catppuccin; \
  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
  tmux display-message 'Theme: catppuccin'"

bind T run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant tmux2k; \
  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
  tmux display-message 'Theme: tmux2k'"

# =============================================================================
# Sesh (tmux session manager)
# =============================================================================

# prefix + g: sesh picker in a tmux popup with fzf
bind-key "g" run-shell "sesh connect \"$(\
  sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
    --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
    --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
    --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
    --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
    --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
    --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
    --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
    --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
    --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
    --preview-window 'right:55%' \
    --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
)\""

bind -N "last-session (via sesh)" S run-shell "sesh last"
bind -N "switch to root session (via sesh)" 9 run-shell "sesh connect --root $(pwd)"

# =============================================================================
# Popup Menu (prefix + Space)
# =============================================================================

unbind-key Space
bind-key Space display-menu -T "#[align=centre,bold]tmux" -x R -y P \
  "Last window" Tab "last-window" \
  "Last pane" '\;' "last-pane" \
  "" "" "" \
  "Choose window" w "choose-tree -Zw" \
  "Choose session" s "choose-tree -Zs" \
  "Show pane numbers" q "display-panes -d 0" \
  "" "" "" \
  "New window" c "new-window -c '#{pane_current_path}'" \
  "Split left/right |" "|" "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'" \
  "Split top/bottom -" "-" "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'" \
  "" "" "" \
  "Pane left" h "select-pane -L" \
  "Pane down" j "select-pane -D" \
  "Pane up" k "select-pane -U" \
  "Pane right" l "select-pane -R" \
  "Zoom toggle" z "resize-pane -Z" \
  "Swap pane left/up" "{" "swap-pane -U" \
  "Swap pane right/down" "}" "swap-pane -D" \
  "" "" "" \
  "Even horizontal (M-1)" E "select-layout even-horizontal" \
  "Even vertical (M-2)" e "select-layout even-vertical" \
  "Main vertical (M-4)" v "select-layout main-vertical" \
  "Main horizontal (M-3)" b "select-layout main-horizontal" \

  "Resize 75%" "+" "resize-pane -x 75%" \
  "" "" "" \
  "Rename session" "$" "command-prompt -I '#S' 'rename-session -- \"%%\"'" \

  "New session" N "command-prompt -p 'New session:' 'new-session -s \"%%\"'" \

Investigating. The "vanilla green" is tmux's default status — strong signal that the `catppuccin/tmux` plugin hasn't actually been loaded. Two likely causes:

1. **Plugin not installed** — TPM auto-clones only when `prefix + I` is pressed, not on reload.
2. **Wrong invocation order** — we set `@catppuccin_*` options but never explicitly `run` the plugin; we rely on TPM's end-of-config `run tpm`, and when `prefix + C` re-sources the config inside an existing server, TPM is idempotent but can still render before our status composition.

Let me check what's installed and fix the theme files + add an auto-install fallback.

# ~/.config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf
# Catppuccin theme with top status bar (inspired by omerxx/dotfiles).

# Declare plugin so TPM keeps it updated
set -g @plugin 'catppuccin/tmux'

# Auto-clone on first use (TPM normally does this only on prefix + I)
if-shell '[ ! -d ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux ]' \
  'run-shell "git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/catppuccin/tmux.git ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux 2>/dev/null"'

# Reset any inherited status styling before Catppuccin composes its own
set -g status-left ""
set -g status-right ""
set -g window-status-format ""
set -g window-status-current-format ""

# Top status bar (omerxx-style)
set -g status-position top

# Catppuccin options (adjust flavor: latte / frappe / macchiato / mocha)
set -g @catppuccin_flavor 'mocha'
set -g @catppuccin_window_status_style 'rounded'
set -g @catppuccin_window_default_fill 'number'
set -g @catppuccin_window_current_fill 'number'
set -g @catppuccin_window_current_text '#{pane_current_command}'
set -g @catppuccin_window_default_text '#W'

# Load plugin explicitly so @catppuccin_status_* modules are defined before
# we reference them below. This is required because prefix + R reloads the
# config without re-running TPM.
run '~/.tmux/plugins/tmux/catppuccin.tmux'

# Compose status line (window list on left after session, system info on right)
set -g status-left "#{E:@catppuccin_status_session} "
set -g status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_application}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_uptime}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_date_time}"

# Explicit window-status formatting so current tab is clearly highlighted
set -g window-status-format "#{E:@catppuccin_window_default_format}"
set -g window-status-current-format "#{E:@catppuccin_window_current_format}"
set -g window-status-separator ""

```

3	Managed tmux config lives under `~/.config/tmux/`, with a shim at `~/.tmux.conf` that sources the XDG entry point. Source layout in this repo:
4	
5	- [`dot_tmux.conf`](../../dot_tmux.conf) → `~/.tmux.conf` (one-line shim)
6	- [`dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf) → entry point, picks theme
7	- [`dot_config/tmux/common.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf) → plugins + theme-agnostic options
8	- [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf) → all bind-keys and popup menu
9	- [`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf) → default theme (top status bar)
10	- [`dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf) → alternative theme (bottom status bar)
11	
12	This setup is tuned for coding-agent and Neovim workflows:
13	
14	- native popup menu on `prefix + Space`
15	- Catppuccin (default, top status bar) or `tmux2k` (bottom) — switchable at runtime
16	- vim-style pane navigation and copy mode
17	- URL opening via fzf (`prefix + u`) and tmux-open in copy mode
18	- capture pane to clipboard helpers
19	- sesh integration for session picking
20	- `extended-keys` enabled with `csi-u` so keys like `Ctrl+/` reach Neovim inside tmux
21	- OSC 52 clipboard and OSC passthrough enabled
22	
23	## Reload Config
24	
25	Most tmux changes do not require restarting the server.
26	
27	Reload the config with either:
28	
29	```bash
30	tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf
31	```
32	
33	Or inside tmux:
34	
35	```text
36	prefix + R
37	```
38	
39	`prefix + R` is the fastest day-to-day option and shows a confirmation message after reloading.
40	
41	If a change still does not behave correctly, try opening a new pane or window first. Only restart the tmux server when a terminal capability or plugin initialization issue clearly survives a reload.
42	
43	## Exit vs Detach
44	
45	- `prefix + d`: detach the current client, leaving the session running
46	- `exit`: close the current shell; when the last pane exits, the session ends
47	- `prefix + :` then `kill-session`: kill the current session immediately
48	- `tmux kill-server`: kill every tmux session and stop the server
49	
50	This config sets `detach-on-destroy off`, so if other sessions still exist, tmux stays open and switches to one of them after you kill the current session.
51	
52	## Prefix Key
53	
54	The prefix remains tmux's default:
55	
56	```text
57	Ctrl + b
58	```
59	
60	Examples below assume `prefix = Ctrl + b`.
61	
62	## Common Keybindings
63	
64	### Daily Workflow
65	
66	| Keybinding | Action |
67	|------------|--------|
68	| `prefix + R` | Reload `~/.tmux.conf` |
69	| `prefix + Space` | Open the tmux popup menu |
70	| `prefix + g` | Open sesh picker |
71	| `prefix + S` | Jump to the last sesh session |
72	| `prefix + 9` | Jump to the git root session for the current repo |
73	| `prefix + N` | New session (prompts for name) |
74	| `prefix + X` | Kill session (with confirmation) |
75	| `prefix + d` | Detach |
76	| `prefix + t` | Show tmux clock mode |
77	| `prefix + C` | Switch theme to Catppuccin (top status bar) |
78	| `prefix + T` | Switch theme to tmux2k (bottom status bar) |
79	
80	### Panes and Windows
81	
82	| Keybinding | Action |
83	|------------|--------|
84	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | Move between panes |
85	| `prefix + H/J/K/L` | Resize panes (5 cells, repeatable) |
86	| `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` | Fine resize panes (1 cell, repeatable) |
87	| `prefix + +` | Set current pane to 75% width |
88	| `prefix + \|` | Split left/right (vertical divider) |
89	| `prefix + -` | Split top/bottom (horizontal divider) |
90	| `prefix + c` | New window in current path |
91	| `prefix + x` | Kill pane |
92	| `prefix + z` | Toggle pane zoom |
93	| `prefix + {` | Swap pane with previous (left/up) |
94	| `prefix + }` | Swap pane with next (right/down) |
95	| `prefix + [` | Enter copy mode |
96	
97	Swap-pane swaps the **content** while keeping the **sizes**. So if you have a 75%/25% split and swap, the left pane's content moves to the right (25%) and vice versa -- the proportions stay fixed.
98	
99	### Layouts
100	
101	| Keybinding | Action |
102	|------------|--------|
103	| `M-1` | Even horizontal layout |
104	| `M-2` | Even vertical layout |
105	| `M-3` | Main horizontal layout |
106	| `M-4` | Main vertical layout |
107	| `M-5` | Tiled layout |
108	| `prefix + E` | Spread panes evenly (built-in) |
109	
110	These are tmux built-in `M-1` through `M-5` bindings. They work without prefix; just hold Meta (Alt/Option) and press the number.
111	
112	### Floating Pane (tmux-floax)
113	
114	| Keybinding | Action |
115	|------------|--------|
116	| `prefix + F` | Toggle floating pane (80% width/height) |
117	| `prefix + P` | Open floax popup menu |
118	
119	The floating pane uses a dedicated tmux session named `float` (hidden from sesh picker via blacklist). It inherits the current pane path. Useful for quick terminal tasks without disrupting your layout.
120	
121	### Copy Mode (Vim-Style)
122	
123	Enter copy mode with `prefix + [`. Navigate with vim keys, then:
124	
125	| Key | Action |
126	|-----|--------|
127	| `v` | Begin character selection (visual mode) |
128	| `V` | Select entire line |
129	| `C-v` | Toggle rectangle/block selection |
130	| `y` | Yank selection to system clipboard |
131	| `/` | Search forward |
132	| `?` | Search backward |
133	| `n`/`N` | Next/previous search match |
134	| `g`/`G` | Jump to top/bottom |
135	| `C-u`/`C-d` | Half-page up/down |
136	| `q` or `Escape` | Exit copy mode |
137	
138	Mouse drag in copy mode also copies the selection to clipboard. Double-click selects a word.
139	
140	### URL Opening
141	
142	| Keybinding | Action |
143	|------------|--------|
144	| `prefix + u` | Open fzf popup listing all URLs in the pane (tmux-fzf-url) |
145	
146	In copy-mode (after selecting text with `v`):
147	
148	| Key | Action |
149	|-----|--------|
150	| `o` | Open selected URL/file in default browser/app (tmux-open) |
151	| `C-o` | Open selection in `$EDITOR` |
152	| `S` | Search selection in Google (tmux-open, configurable via `@open-S`) |
153	
154	Typical workflow: `prefix + u` for quick URL browsing; `prefix + [` then select + `o` for precise URL opening.
155	
156	### Capture Pane
157	
158	| Keybinding | Action |
159	|------------|--------|
160	| `prefix + y` | Copy visible pane content to system clipboard |
161	| `prefix + Y` | Copy full scrollback to system clipboard |
162	| `prefix + C-y` | Open scrollback in fzf, select lines to copy (Tab=multi) |
163	
164	Works cross-platform: uses `pbcopy` on macOS, `xclip`/`xsel` on Linux. OSC 52 clipboard also works for the vim-style `y` yank in copy mode (even over SSH).

222	## Coding-Agent / Neovim Notes
223	
224	- `escape-time 0` removes the ESC delay, which helps Neovim feel responsive.
225	- `extended-keys always` with `extended-keys-format csi-u` is what allows `Ctrl+/` and similar modified punctuation keys to pass through tmux more reliably.
226	- The managed Alacritty config also sends `Ctrl+/` as `\u001f`, which matches LazyVim's built-in `<C-_>` fallback for terminal toggle.
227	- `set-clipboard on` enables OSC 52 clipboard copy over SSH.
228	- `allow-passthrough on` helps terminal image protocols and similar passthrough features.
229	
230	If `Ctrl+/` still does not work after `prefix + R`, restart the current terminal app or fully restart tmux once to make sure the terminal capability negotiation is fresh.
231	
232	## Plugins
233	
234	| Plugin | Purpose |
235	|--------|---------|
236	| `tmux-resurrect` | Save/restore sessions across tmux restarts |
237	| `tmux-continuum` | Automatic session saving |
238	| `tmux-floax` | Floating scratch pane (`prefix+F` toggle, `prefix+P` menu) |
239	| `tmux-fzf-url` | `prefix+u` opens fzf popup with all URLs in pane |
240	| `tmux-open` | In copy-mode: `o` opens selection, `C-o` in editor, `S` search |
241	| `catppuccin/tmux` | Status bar theme (mocha, top bar) — default |
242	| `tmux2k` | Status bar theme (onedark, bottom bar) — alternative |
243	
244	Plugins are managed by TPM. Run `prefix + I` to install after first setup.
245	
246	## Themes
247	
248	Two themes are installed; Catppuccin is the default.
249	
250	| Theme | Status bar | Active option |
251	|-------|-----------|---------------|
252	| Catppuccin (mocha, rounded windows) | **top** | `@theme_variant = catppuccin` (default) |
253	| tmux2k (onedark, with git/cpu/ram + bandwidth/network/time) | **bottom** | `@theme_variant = tmux2k` |
254	
255	### How theme selection works
256	
257	The entry point `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` resolves the theme in this order:
258	
259	1. `TMUX_THEME` environment variable (if set when tmux starts).
260	2. The `@theme_variant` tmux option (persisted on the server until `kill-server`).
261	3. Fallback: `catppuccin`.
262	
263	### Switching
264	
265	- **Per-server at launch** (shell-side):
266	
267	  ```bash
268	  TMUX_THEME=tmux2k tmux        # start tmux in tmux2k
269	  TMUX_THEME=catppuccin tmux    # start tmux in catppuccin
270	  ```
271	
272	  Handy aliases if you want a one-letter command:
273	
274	  ```bash
275	  alias tmuxc='TMUX_THEME=catppuccin tmux'
276	  alias tmuxt='TMUX_THEME=tmux2k tmux'
277	  ```
278	
279	- **Inside a running session**:
280	
281	  | Keybinding | Action |
282	  |------------|--------|
283	  | `prefix + C` | Switch to Catppuccin |
284	  | `prefix + T` | Switch to tmux2k |
285	
286	  Both entries also live in the `prefix + Space` popup menu.
287	
288	- **First-time switch caveat**: each theme file only declares its own TPM plugin, so the other theme may not be installed yet the first time you flip. After switching, press `prefix + I` to let TPM clone it. For the cleanest visual result (no leftover style from the previous theme), run `tmux kill-server && tmux`.
289	
290	## Tmux × Vim / Neovim
291	
292	Yes -- the current config already gives you vi-style scroll and copy. It sets `mode-keys vi`, and the **Copy Mode (Vim-Style)** table above lists the full key set (`v`, `V`, `C-v`, `y`, `g`/`G`, `/`, `?`, `C-u`/`C-d`). Enter with `prefix + [`, exit with `q`.
293	
294	Other bits already wired for Neovim:
295	
296	- `escape-time 0` — no ESC delay.
297	- `focus-events on` — Vim's `autoread` and Neovim's `FocusGained` / `FocusLost` fire correctly.
298	- `default-terminal tmux-256color` + `terminal-features ...:RGB` — true color inside tmux.
299	- `extended-keys always` + CSI-u — `Ctrl+/`, `Shift+Enter`, `Ctrl+Enter` etc. reach Neovim through tmux.
300	- `set-clipboard on` — OSC 52 yanks from copy mode work over SSH.
301	
302	Possible future add-on (not installed): [`christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator`](https://github.com/christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator) for prefix-less `Ctrl+h/j/k/l` navigation across tmux panes and Vim splits. Would replace the current `prefix + h/j/k/l` bindings if adopted.
303	
304	For broader workflow patterns, see [Tmux and Vim — even better together](https://smartbear.com/blog/tmux-and-vim/) in Resources below.
305	
306	## Troubleshooting
307	
308	### Bandwidth segment shows `18446744073709551615K` (tmux2k)
309	
310	That number is `2^64 − 1` — the uint64 wraparound value. It appears when tmux2k's bandwidth helper computes `previous_counter − current_counter` and the subtraction underflows. Common triggers:
311	
312	- tmux2k's auto-detected interface has no traffic or disappeared (VPN tunnel, `docker0`, a bridge interface, etc.).
313	- The cached "previous tick" counter is missing on the first refresh after a reload or server restart.
314	
315	Workarounds (pick one):
316	
317	1. **Switch to Catppuccin**: `prefix + C` — the default theme doesn't render a bandwidth segment at all.
318	2. **Pin the interface** in `dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf`:
319	
320	   ```tmux
321	   set -g @tmux2k-network-name "en0"       # macOS Wi-Fi
322	   # set -g @tmux2k-network-name "wlan0"   # typical Linux Wi-Fi
323	   # set -g @tmux2k-network-name "eth0"    # typical Linux wired
324	   ```
325	
326	   Find the right name with `ip -br link` (Linux) or `ifconfig` / `networksetup -listallhardwareports` (macOS).
327	3. **Drop the bandwidth segment**: remove `bandwidth` from `@tmux2k-right-plugins`, keeping only `network time`.
328	
329	See upstream [2kabhishek/tmux2k](https://github.com/2kabhishek/tmux2k) issues for progress.
330

# tmux

Managed tmux config lives under `~/.config/tmux/`, with a shim at `~/.tmux.conf` that sources the XDG entry point.

## Source layout (in this repo)

| Source | Deployed | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| [`dot_tmux.conf`](../../../dot_tmux.conf) | `~/.tmux.conf` | one-line shim |
| [`dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf) | `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` | entry point, picks theme |
| [`dot_config/tmux/common.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf) | — | plugins + theme-agnostic options |
| [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf) | — | all bind-keys and popup menu |
| [`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf) | — | default theme (top status bar) |
| [`dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf) | — | alternative theme (bottom status bar) |

This setup is tuned for coding-agent and Neovim workflows:

- native popup menu on `prefix + Space`
- Catppuccin (default, top status bar) or tmux2k (bottom) — switchable at runtime
- vim-style pane navigation and copy mode
- URL opening via fzf (`prefix + u`) and tmux-open in copy mode
- capture pane to clipboard helpers
- sesh integration for session picking
- `extended-keys` with `csi-u` so keys like `Ctrl+/` reach Neovim inside tmux
- OSC 52 clipboard and OSC passthrough enabled

## In this folder

- [keybindings.md](./keybindings.md) — all keybindings and the popup menu
- [themes.md](./themes.md) — Catppuccin / tmux2k selection, switching, troubleshooting
- [vim.md](./vim.md) — tmux × Vim/Neovim notes and external resources

## First-time setup

After `chezmoi apply`, start tmux and run `prefix + I` once to let TPM install the plugins. The theme files also auto-clone their plugin on first source as a safety net, but TPM is the canonical installer.

## Reload Config

Most changes do not need a server restart.

\```bash
tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf
\```

Or, inside tmux: `prefix + R` (shows a confirmation message after reloading).

If a change still behaves wrong, try a new pane/window first. Only `tmux kill-server` when a terminal-capability or plugin-init issue clearly survives a reload — e.g. switching themes without leftover styling.

## Exit vs Detach

- `prefix + d` — detach the current client, leaving the session running
- `exit` — close the current shell; when the last pane exits, the session ends
- `prefix + :` then `kill-session` — kill the current session immediately
- `tmux kill-server` — kill every session and stop the server

`detach-on-destroy off` is set, so when you kill a session tmux switches to another one instead of detaching if other sessions exist.

## Prefix Key

Default: `Ctrl + b`. Examples in the sibling docs assume `prefix = Ctrl + b`.

## Plugins

| Plugin | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `tmux-resurrect` | Save/restore sessions across tmux restarts |
| `tmux-continuum` | Automatic session saving |
| `tmux-floax` | Floating scratch pane (`prefix+F` toggle, `prefix+P` menu) |
| `tmux-fzf-url` | `prefix+u` opens fzf popup with all URLs in pane |
| `tmux-open` | In copy-mode: `o` opens selection, `C-o` in editor, `S` search |
| `catppuccin/tmux` | Status bar theme (mocha, top bar) — default |
| `tmux2k` | Status bar theme (onedark, bottom bar) — alternative |

Managed by TPM; `prefix + I` to install, `prefix + U` to update.

## Verify current config

\```bash
ls ~/.config/tmux/
tmux display-message -p '#{@theme_variant}'
tmux list-keys -T prefix
tmux show-options -s | rg 'extended-keys|extended-keys-format|default-terminal'
tmux show-options -g | rg 'status|focus-events'
\```

## Related Docs

- [Sesh](../sesh.md)
- [Starship](../starship.md)

All bindings use the default prefix `Ctrl + b`.

| `prefix + T` | Switch theme to tmux2k (bottom status bar) |

## Panes and Windows

| Keybinding | Action |
|------------|--------|

| `prefix + H/J/K/L` | Resize panes (5 cells, repeatable) |
| `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` | Fine resize panes (1 cell, repeatable) |
| `prefix + +` | Set current pane to 75% width |
| `prefix + \|` | Split left/right (vertical divider) |
| `prefix + -` | Split top/bottom (horizontal divider) |
| `prefix + c` | New window in current path |

| `prefix + }` | Swap pane with next (right/down) |

Swap-pane swaps the **content** while keeping the **sizes**. So if you have a 75%/25% split and swap, the left pane's content moves to the right (25%) and vice versa — the proportions stay fixed.

## Layouts

`M-1` through `M-5` are tmux built-ins — no prefix needed; just hold Meta (Alt/Option) and press the number.

## Floating Pane (tmux-floax)

Enter with `prefix + [`. Navigate with vim keys, then:

| `V` | Select entire line |

| `y` | Yank selection to system clipboard |
| `/` | Search forward |
| `?` | Search backward |
| `n`/`N` | Next/previous search match |
| `g`/`G` | Jump to top/bottom |
| `C-u`/`C-d` | Half-page up/down |
| `q` or `Escape` | Exit copy mode |

Mouse drag in copy mode also copies to clipboard. Double-click selects a word.

## URL Opening

| Keybinding | Action |
|------------|--------|
| `prefix + u` | Open fzf popup listing all URLs in the pane (tmux-fzf-url) |

In copy-mode (after selecting text with `v`):

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `o` | Open selected URL/file in default browser/app (tmux-open) |
| `C-o` | Open selection in `$EDITOR` |
| `S` | Search selection in Google (tmux-open, configurable via `@open-S`) |

Typical workflow: `prefix + u` for quick URL browsing; `prefix + [` then select + `o` for precise URL opening.

## Capture Pane

| Keybinding | Action |
|------------|--------|
| `prefix + y` | Copy visible pane content to system clipboard |
| `prefix + Y` | Copy full scrollback to system clipboard |
| `prefix + C-y` | Open scrollback in fzf, select lines to copy (Tab=multi) |

Cross-platform: `pbcopy` on macOS, `xclip`/`xsel` on Linux. OSC 52 also works for the vim-style `y` yank (even over SSH).

## Built-in tmux Keys Still Available

| Keybinding | Action |
|------------|--------|
| `prefix + s` | Choose session tree |
| `prefix + w` | Choose window tree |
| `prefix + q` | Show pane numbers |
| `prefix + ,` | Rename window |
| `prefix + $` | Rename session |
| `prefix + ?` | List named keybindings |
| `prefix + /` | Prompt for a key and show what it is bound to |

## Popup Menu (`prefix + Space`)

Menu accelerator keys match the standalone `prefix + key` bindings wherever possible — pressing `R` inside the menu does the same thing as `prefix + R` outside it. Items marked "menu-only" have no standalone binding.

| Key | Action | Also works as `prefix + key`? |
|-----|--------|-------------------------------|
| `;` | Last pane | yes (built-in) |
| `w` | Choose window | yes (built-in) |
| `s` | Choose session | yes (built-in) |
| `q` | Show pane numbers | yes (built-in) |
| `c` | New window | yes |
| `\|` | Split left/right | yes |
| `-` | Split top/bottom | yes |
| `h/j/k/l` | Navigate panes | yes |
| `z` | Zoom toggle | yes (built-in) |
| `{` / `}` | Swap pane left-up / right-down | yes (built-in) |
| `E/e/v/b/T` | Layout presets | menu-only (use `M-1`..`M-5`) |
| `+` | Resize pane to 75% width | yes |
| `$` | Rename session | yes (built-in) |
| `,` | Rename window | yes (built-in) |
| `N` | New session | yes |
| `x` | Kill pane (confirm) | yes |
| `X` | Kill session (confirm) | yes |
| `Q` | Kill all sessions / server | menu-only |
| `C` | Theme: Catppuccin (top bar) | yes |
| `M` | Theme: tmux2k (bottom bar) | yes (bound to `prefix + T`) |
| `g` | Sesh picker | yes |
| `S` | Last sesh session | yes |
| `9` | Sesh git root | yes |
| `R` | Reload config | yes |

| `d` | Detach | yes (built-in) |
| `t` | Clock | yes (built-in) |
| `?` | List keys | yes (built-in) |

# tmux — Themes

Two themes are installed side-by-side; **Catppuccin is the default**.

| Theme | Status bar | Active option |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Catppuccin (mocha, rounded windows) | **top** | `@theme_variant = catppuccin` (default) |
| tmux2k (onedark, with git / cpu / ram + bandwidth / network / time) | **bottom** | `@theme_variant = tmux2k` |

## How theme selection works

The entry point `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` resolves the theme in this order:

1. `TMUX_THEME` environment variable (if set when tmux starts).
2. The `@theme_variant` tmux option (persists on the server until `kill-server`).
3. Fallback: `catppuccin`.

Each theme file declares its own TPM plugin, explicitly `run`s that plugin (so `prefix + R` works), and resets `status-left/right` + `window-status-format` before composing its own.

## Switching

### Per-server at launch (shell-side)

\```bash
TMUX_THEME=tmux2k tmux        # start tmux in tmux2k
TMUX_THEME=catppuccin tmux    # start tmux in catppuccin
\```

Handy aliases:

\```bash
alias tmuxc='TMUX_THEME=catppuccin tmux'
alias tmuxt='TMUX_THEME=tmux2k tmux'
\```

### Inside a running session

| Keybinding | Action |
|------------|--------|
| `prefix + C` | Switch to Catppuccin |
| `prefix + T` | Switch to tmux2k |

Both entries also live in the `prefix + Space` popup menu.

### First-time caveat

Only the active theme's plugin is declared to TPM at config load time. The first time you flip to the other theme, the theme file's auto-clone hook fetches the repo, then the explicit `run` loads it. If the status bar still looks off after `prefix + C` / `prefix + T`:

1. Press `prefix + I` — TPM will (re)install anything missing.
2. For the cleanest visual result (no leftover style from the previous theme), run `tmux kill-server && tmux`.

## Troubleshooting

### Catppuccin shows default green tmux status bar

Means the plugin isn't loaded. Check:

\```bash
ls ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux   # should contain catppuccin.tmux
\```

If missing, the auto-clone didn't run (e.g. no network on first reload). Fix:

\```bash
git clone https://github.com/catppuccin/tmux.git ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux
tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf
\```

Or just press `prefix + I` once inside tmux.

### Bandwidth segment shows `18446744073709551615K` (tmux2k)

That number is `2^64 − 1` — the uint64 wraparound value. It appears when tmux2k's bandwidth helper computes `previous_counter − current_counter` and the subtraction underflows. Common triggers:

- tmux2k's auto-detected interface has no traffic or disappeared (VPN tunnel, `docker0`, a bridge interface, etc.).
- The cached "previous tick" counter is missing on the first refresh after a reload or server restart.

Workarounds (pick one):

1. **Switch to Catppuccin**: `prefix + C` — the default theme doesn't render a bandwidth segment at all.
2. **Pin the interface** in `dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf`:

   \```tmux
   set -g @tmux2k-network-name "en0"       # macOS Wi-Fi
   # set -g @tmux2k-network-name "wlan0"   # typical Linux Wi-Fi
   # set -g @tmux2k-network-name "eth0"    # typical Linux wired
   \```

   Find the right name with `ip -br link` (Linux) or `ifconfig` / `networksetup -listallhardwareports` (macOS).
3. **Drop the bandwidth segment**: remove `bandwidth` from `@tmux2k-right-plugins`, keeping only `network time`.

See upstream [2kabhishek/tmux2k](https://github.com/2kabhishek/tmux2k) issues for progress.

### Switching themes leaves residual styling

Some tmux options (colors, pane-border-style, etc.) persist on the server after a plugin sets them. Our theme files reset `status-left/right` and `window-status-*` before composing, which covers the visible status bar, but deeper style overrides may linger. Cleanest workaround:

\```bash
tmux kill-server && tmux
\```

```

# tmux × Vim / Neovim

## Vi copy / scroll — already on

The current config sets `mode-keys vi`, so scroll and copy mode behave vim-style out of the box:

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `prefix + [` | Enter copy mode |
| `h/j/k/l` | Move cursor |
| `C-u` / `C-d` | Half-page up/down |
| `g` / `G` | Top / bottom |
| `/` / `?` | Search forward / backward |
| `v` / `V` / `C-v` | Char / line / rectangle selection |
| `y` | Yank to system clipboard (OSC 52) |
| `q` or `Escape` | Exit |

See [keybindings.md → Copy Mode](./keybindings.md#copy-mode-vim-style) for the full table.

## Neovim-friendly settings already in `common.conf`

- `escape-time 0` — no ESC delay, Neovim feels responsive.
- `focus-events on` — Vim's `autoread` and Neovim's `FocusGained` / `FocusLost` fire correctly.
- `default-terminal tmux-256color` + `terminal-features ...:RGB` — true color inside tmux.
- `extended-keys always` + `extended-keys-format csi-u` — `Ctrl+/`, `Shift+Enter`, `Ctrl+Enter` etc. reach Neovim through tmux.
- `set-clipboard on` — OSC 52 yanks from copy mode work over SSH.
- `allow-passthrough on` — helps terminal image protocols and similar passthrough features.

If `Ctrl+/` still does not work after `prefix + R`, restart the terminal app or `tmux kill-server` once so terminal capability negotiation is fresh. The managed Alacritty config sends `Ctrl+/` as `\u001f`, which matches LazyVim's built-in `<C-_>` fallback for terminal toggle.

## Possible future add-on

[`christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator`](https://github.com/christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator) — prefix-less `Ctrl+h/j/k/l` navigation that seamlessly crosses tmux panes and Vim splits. Not installed; adopting it would replace the current `prefix + h/j/k/l` bindings.

## Resources

- [rothgar/awesome-tmux](https://github.com/rothgar/awesome-tmux) — curated list of tmux plugins, themes, and articles.
- [Tmux and Vim — even better together (SmartBear)](https://smartbear.com/blog/tmux-and-vim/) — workflow patterns for pairing tmux with Vim/Neovim.
- [omerxx/dotfiles — tmux/](https://github.com/omerxx/dotfiles/tree/master/tmux) — reference config with Catppuccin + top status bar (see [video walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GH3kpsbbERo)).

```

## Fixes applied

**Catppuccin render fix** — root cause was the `catppuccin/tmux` plugin was never cloned (TPM only installs on `prefix + I`, not on reload, and on `prefix + C` switching). Fixes in `theme.catppuccin.conf`:
- Added **auto-clone** via `if-shell` when `~/.tmux/plugins/tmux/` is missing.
- Added **explicit `run '~/.tmux/plugins/tmux/catppuccin.tmux'`** after setting options, so `@catppuccin_status_*` modules are defined before we reference them (previously relied on TPM at end of config, which doesn't re-run on `prefix + R`).
- Added explicit `window-status-format` / `window-status-current-format` so the active tab is clearly highlighted.
- I also cloned catppuccin into `~/.tmux/plugins/tmux/` now, so after `chezmoi apply` + `prefix + R` it should render correctly without any manual step.

**tmux2k parallel fix** — its entry script is `2k.tmux` (not `tmux2k.tmux`). Added explicit `run '~/.tmux/plugins/tmux2k/2k.tmux'` + auto-clone so `prefix + T` works after a reload too.

## Docs reorganized

Old `docs/tools/tmux.md` deleted; new folder `docs/tools/tmux/`:
- `README.md` — overview, source layout, plugins, reload, verify
- `keybindings.md` — all key tables + popup menu
- `themes.md` — Catppuccin/tmux2k selection, switching, troubleshooting (including new "Catppuccin shows default green" entry and the bandwidth UINT64 bug)
- `vim.md` — tmux × Vim notes + external resources

CLAUDE.md and README.md updated to point at the new folder.

**To verify:** `chezmoi apply` then inside tmux `prefix + R` — Catppuccin top bar with highlighted active window should render. If not, `tmux kill-server && tmux`.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-6 2026-04-15 05:05:01Z)**_

Found it. Catppuccin v2 (what got cloned) auto-sets `window-status-format` when the plugin runs — but I'm **overriding** it afterwards with variable names that don't exist in v2 (`@catppuccin_window_default_format` / `@catppuccin_window_current_format`), so the window list gets blanked. tmux2k works because it composes its own status line without that problem.

```conf
# ~/.config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf
# Catppuccin theme with top status bar.

# Declare plugin so TPM keeps it updated on prefix + U
set -g @plugin 'catppuccin/tmux'

# Auto-clone on first use (TPM only installs on prefix + I)
if-shell '[ ! -d ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux ]' \
  'run-shell "git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/catppuccin/tmux.git ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux 2>/dev/null"'

# Top status bar
set -g status-position top

# Catppuccin options -- must be set BEFORE running the plugin
set -g @catppuccin_flavor 'mocha'
set -g @catppuccin_window_status_style 'rounded'

# Window text (what each tab shows). #I = index, #W = window name, #T = pane title
set -g @catppuccin_window_text ' #W'
set -g @catppuccin_window_current_text ' #W'
set -g @catppuccin_window_number_position 'left'

# Load plugin -- this populates @catppuccin_status_*, window-status-format,
# window-status-current-format with Catppuccin styling
run '~/.tmux/plugins/tmux/catppuccin.tmux'

# Compose status line AFTER the plugin has defined its modules
set -g status-left ""
set -g status-right ""
set -agF status-left "#{E:@catppuccin_status_session}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_application}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_uptime}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_date_time}"

# NOTE: intentionally do NOT override window-status-format /
# window-status-current-format here -- the plugin has already set those based
# on @catppuccin_window_status_style above, and overriding them with
# non-existent v1 variables wipes the window list.

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-6 2026-04-15 06:01:38Z)**_

Confirmed — with the fix, Catppuccin now populates `window-status-format` properly (rounded, colored, showing `#I` index + `#W` name). The previous config wiped it by overriding with v1-era variable names that don't exist in v2.

## What was wrong and what's fixed

- **Window list vanished** because the old `theme.catppuccin.conf` overrode `window-status-format` / `window-status-current-format` with `#{E:@catppuccin_window_default_format}` and `#{E:@catppuccin_window_current_format}` — these are v1 variable names that don't exist in Catppuccin v2. v2's plugin sets those format options itself based on `@catppuccin_window_status_style`, so any post-run override wipes the list.
- **Fix**: removed the bogus overrides. The plugin now controls window rendering. Also added `@catppuccin_window_text`, `@catppuccin_window_current_text`, `@catppuccin_window_number_position` for tweakable tab text.

## What you need to do

Apply and reload:

```bash
chezmoi apply
# inside tmux:
# prefix + R    (or tmux kill-server && tmux for a truly clean render)
```

Then `prefix + c` to open a few windows — you should see rounded colored tabs with index + name, with the active one highlighted in mauve. If you want a different accent color, change `@catppuccin_flavor` (`mocha` / `macchiato` / `frappe` / `latte`) in `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`.

About `prefix + I`: the reason it didn't list `catppuccin/tmux` or `tmux2k` is that those `@plugin` declarations live in the theme files (only the active one is declared), so TPM only sees the non-theme plugins. The theme plugins are handled by our auto-clone + explicit `run` instead — working as designed, just cosmetically quiet in TPM's output.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-6 2026-04-15 06:07:59Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-6 2026-04-15 06:08:06Z)**_

**On the approach**: yes, it's more robust than pure TPM for our case — three concrete benefits:

1. **Reload-safe**: `prefix + R` re-sources the theme file and re-runs the plugin, so switching themes inside a session actually re-renders. Pure TPM only loads plugins when `run tpm` fires at end-of-config, which behaves inconsistently on subsequent reloads.
2. **First-boot works without manual install**: the auto-clone check means a fresh `chezmoi apply` + `tmux` produces a styled bar immediately, no `prefix + I` step.
3. **Only one theme activates at a time**: declaring `@plugin` inside each theme file (not in common) means TPM won't load both plugins simultaneously and have them fight for `status-left`/`status-right`.

**Tradeoffs**: TPM's `prefix + I` output is quieter (doesn't list theme plugins); `prefix + U` won't update them either — upgrades need a manual `cd ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux && git pull`. Acceptable since theme plugins are stable.

Found both issues:

**1. Bitwarden SSH agent is locked / refusing**
```
get_agent_identities: ssh_fetch_identitylist: agent refused operation
```
The agent is connected (via `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`) but refusing to hand over keys — typical symptom of Bitwarden being locked. Fix: `bw unlock` (or click the Bitwarden desktop icon to unlock), then retry.

**2. `~/.ssh/config.d/01_git` is never loaded**
The debug output reads only `/home/daviddwlee84/.ssh/config` — there's no `Include config.d/*` in the main config, so your `01_git` (with `IdentitiesOnly yes`) is dead code right now. The main config's `Host github.com` block is what's applied, and it lacks `IdentitiesOnly yes`. Not fatal for the current failure, but worth fixing — add `Include config.d/*` at the top of `~/.ssh/config`.

**3. The actual connection-drop cause**
SSH offers `jingle` (RSA key, `SHA256:B7ZcVqELH0RQ4YvcDOdEl9ImxJHeS3XZR8PaatW3Tcw`) and GitHub immediately closes. Two possibilities:

- **That specific key isn't registered on GitHub** — dropping right after one offer with no "permission denied" is unusual but happens with GFW interference on the China endpoint `20.205.243.166`.
- **GFW mid-stream reset** — the China GitHub endpoint often resets port-22 SSH mid-auth.

Port 443 gives a clean **`Permission denied (publickey)`** — no GFW issue, the network is fine.

The real problem is the Bitwarden SSH agent being locked:

- With BW unlocked: agent offers its stored keys → one of them is registered on GitHub → auth succeeds.
- With BW locked (current state): agent refuses → SSH falls back to `~/.ssh/jingle` (RSA, `B7ZcVq…W3Tcw`) → **that specific key file isn't registered on your GitHub account** → denied.

Your "jingle" key that works is probably stored **inside Bitwarden**, not as `~/.ssh/jingle` on disk. They're two different things sharing a name.

### To push now

1. Unlock Bitwarden (open the desktop app and unlock, or `bw unlock` in a shell where `BW_SESSION` then gets exported).
2. Verify agent sees keys: `ssh-add -l` — should list the Bitwarden-held key.
3. `git push`.

### Optional cleanup

Add `Include config.d/*` at the top of `~/.ssh/config` so your modular `config.d/01_git` actually takes effect — right now the main config's `github.com` block shadows it and lacks `IdentitiesOnly yes`.

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Right-click menu fix + Catppuccin polish + XDG docs

## Context

Follow-up pass on the modular tmux config from the previous commit. User hit three issues:

1. **Right-click popup menu vanishes on mouse release** — when right-clicking in a pane, the menu appears briefly but dismisses the moment the mouse button is released, so no item can be selected.
2. **Catppuccin window tabs are centered** — user wants them left-aligned, and wants more useful modules on the status bar than just `session / application / uptime / date_time`.
3. **No docs on XDG Base Directory Specification** — useful background for why `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` is preferred over `~/.tmux.conf`, and applies to many other configs in this repo.

## Findings

### Right-click menu dismissal

tmux 3.4's built-in `MouseDown3Pane` / `MouseDown3Status` / `MouseDown3StatusLeft` bindings invoke `display-menu` **without** the `-O` flag. Without `-O`, `display-menu` closes if the mouse is released outside an item before a selection is made — which is exactly what happens on a quick right-click-and-release. Adding `-O` ("stay **O**pen until an item is chosen or Escape") makes the menu persist as expected.

Confirmed via `tmux list-keys -T root | grep MouseDown3` — our config doesn't override these; we're getting tmux defaults minus `-O`.

### Catppuccin alignment + modules

- Alignment: `set -g status-justify centre` (tmux default) is what centers the window list. Change to `left`.
- v2 plugin at `~/.tmux/plugins/tmux/status/` ships these modules: `application`, `battery`, `clima`, `cpu`, `date_time`, `directory`, `gitmux`, `host`, `kube`, `load`, `pomodoro_plus`, `ram`, `session`, `uptime`, `user`, `weather`. Our current theme only uses 4 (`session`, `application`, `uptime`, `date_time`).

Useful additions that don't need extra tooling:
- `directory` — current pane's `pwd` (basename). Very useful when juggling repos.
- `host` — hostname. Handy when SSH'd into many boxes.
- `user` — `$USER`. Cheap situational awareness.
- `cpu` / `ram` — already covered by tmux2k for users who want sysload; optional in catppuccin.
- `battery` — only meaningful on laptops (macOS / Linux with power); gracefully shows nothing otherwise.

Proposed composition:
- **Left**: `session` → `directory`  (what am I in)
- **Right**: `application` → `user` `@` `host` → `date_time`  (what's running, where, when)

Keep it minimal by default; document the full module list so user can remix.

### XDG Base Directory docs

No existing doc. Most tools in this repo already use XDG paths (`~/.config/nvim`, `~/.config/zellij`, etc.), and the tmux refactor just moved to `~/.config/tmux/`. A short `docs/tools/xdg.md` explaining the spec and listing where our configs live fits the existing `docs/tools/*.md` pattern.

## Changes

### 1. `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` — right-click menu fix

Add, near the top of the file, a block that rebinds the three root-level MouseDown3 events with `-O`:

```tmux
# =============================================================================
# Mouse menu persistence (fix: menu dismisses on mouse release without -O)
# =============================================================================

unbind-key -n MouseDown3Pane
bind-key -n MouseDown3Pane \
  if-shell -F -t = "#{||:#{mouse_any_flag},#{&&:#{pane_in_mode},#{?#{m/r:(copy|view)-mode,#{pane_mode}},0,1}}}" \
    { select-pane -t = ; send-keys -M } \
    { display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{pane_index} (#{pane_id})" -t = -x M -y M \
        "Horizontal Split" h { split-window -h } \
        "Vertical Split"   v { split-window -v } \
        "" \
        "Swap Up"     u { swap-pane -U } \
        "Swap Down"   d { swap-pane -D } \
        "" \
        "#{?window_zoomed_flag,Unzoom,Zoom}" z { resize-pane -Z } \
        "Kill pane"   X { kill-pane } \
        "Respawn"     R { respawn-pane -k } }

unbind-key -n MouseDown3Status
bind-key -n MouseDown3Status \
  display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{window_index}:#{window_name}" -t = -x W -y W \
    "Swap Left"  l { swap-window -t :-1 } \
    "Swap Right" r { swap-window -t :+1 } \
    "" \
    "Kill window" X { kill-window } \
    "Rename"      n { command-prompt -F -I "#W" { rename-window -t "#{window_id}" "%%" } } \
    "" \
    "New window"  w { new-window }

unbind-key -n MouseDown3StatusLeft
bind-key -n MouseDown3StatusLeft \
  display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{session_name}" -t = -x M -y W \
    Next        n { switch-client -n } \
    Previous    p { switch-client -p } \
    "" \
    Rename      N { command-prompt -I "#S" { rename-session "%%" } } \
    "" \
    "New session" s { new-session } \
    "New window"  w { new-window }
```

Simplified versus tmux defaults (dropped the copy-mode-specific items and the "mouse word / line / hyperlink" helpers) for readability; users who want that richness can fall back to `prefix + Space`. The important bit is the `-O` flag.

### 2. Left-align windows — Catppuccin only

Per user preference: Catppuccin = left, tmux2k = keep centered (habitual).

- `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`: add `set -g status-justify left`
- `dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf`: add `set -g status-justify centre` (explicit reset, so switching Catppuccin → tmux2k on the same server doesn't leak `left`)
- `common.conf`: no change

### 3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — richer modules

Replace the current status composition with:

```tmux
set -g status-left ""
set -g status-right ""

# Left: session + directory
set -agF status-left "#{E:@catppuccin_status_session}"
set -agF status-left "#{E:@catppuccin_status_directory}"

# Right: application, user@host, date/time
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_application}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_user}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_host}"
set -agF status-right "#{E:@catppuccin_status_date_time}"

# Module tweaks
set -g @catppuccin_directory_text "#{b:pane_current_path}"   # basename only
set -g @catppuccin_date_time_text "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"
```

Drop `uptime` (noisy, rarely useful). Keep settings minimal; the long list of available modules lives in docs so users can add battery/cpu/gitmux/weather by uncommenting examples.

### 4. `docs/tools/xdg.md` — new

Single-page primer:

- What XDG Base Directory Specification is, link to [freedesktop spec](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir/latest/).
- The four core vars: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (`~/.config`), `XDG_DATA_HOME` (`~/.local/share`), `XDG_STATE_HOME` (`~/.local/state`), `XDG_CACHE_HOME` (`~/.cache`).
- Why it matters: keeps `$HOME` clean, predictable tooling, easy to back up / sync / delete.
- Table of **this repo's** config locations, with a column noting whether each tool honors XDG natively or needs a shim. Good ones to list: tmux (native in 3.1+, we use shim `~/.tmux.conf` → `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf`), neovim, zellij, starship, alacritty, ghostty, yazi, bat, direnv, gh, claude (some still use `~/.*`).
- Short "how this repo handles it" note pointing at `dot_config/` vs dotfiles in `$HOME`.

### 5. `docs/tools/tmux/README.md` — link to XDG doc

Add under "Related Docs":

```markdown
- [XDG Base Directory Specification](../xdg.md) — why configs live under `~/.config/tmux/` rather than `~/.tmux.conf`
```

### 6. `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md` — document the mouse menu behavior

Add a short "Right-click menus" subsection under the existing mouse content, explaining that right-click opens a context menu on panes (`MouseDown3Pane`), the window list (`MouseDown3Status`), and session area (`MouseDown3StatusLeft`), and that they stay open until Escape or selection.

### 7. `docs/tools/tmux/themes.md` — catalog Catppuccin modules

Add a section listing every available module from `~/.tmux/plugins/tmux/status/` with a one-line description and a toggle-on example so users can remix. Also note the `@catppuccin_directory_text`, `@catppuccin_date_time_text` knobs.

## Files touched

**Modified:**
- `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` — add `-O` mouse rebindings
- `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `status-justify left`, richer modules, directory/user/host

## Verification

1. `chezmoi apply`
2. In a fresh tmux (cleanest: `tmux kill-server && tmux`):
   - Right-click in a pane → menu opens, stays open on mouse release, Escape or selection to close. Repeat on the window list and the session area on the left of the status bar.
   - Window tabs are left-aligned right after the session segment.
